3.zh:
我們若把嚼環放在馬嘴裡，叫他順服，就能調動他的全身。

**若。**有文本為“且看”。
**嚼環。**或“韁繩”。
**馬嘴。**馬可能是最活躍的家畜了，但只需一個小小裝置放在它嘴裡，就能控制它的全部行動。
**順服。**脫韁的馬會危及騎手的生命，同樣，不受約束的舌頭也會危害整個基督徒經驗。人和對家畜都需要順從和控制。
**全身。**見2節註釋。
3.en:
**Behold.** Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading “now if.”
Bits. Or, “bridles.”
Horses’ mouths. A horse is perhaps the most spirited of domestic animals, but it takes only a small mechanism in the mouth to control all its actions.
Obey. As an unruly horse endangers the life of its rider, so an unruly tongue jeopardizes the whole Christian experience. Obedience and control are desirable for men as well as for domesticated animals.
Whole body. See on v. 2.

4.zh:
看哪，船隻雖然甚大，又被大風催逼，只用小小的舵，就隨著掌舵的意思轉動。

**船隻。**雅各的許多讀者都熟悉船隻，因為羅馬帝國位於地中海邊。
**甚大。**古代的船隻在那時的人看來似乎很大，但現在的遠洋班輪要大得多了。保羅到馬耳他是乘一艘大船，共載了276個人，包括船員和乘客（見徒27:37）。但任何船隻與控制它的舵相比都是龐大的。
**大。**sklēros，“嚴的”，“強的”，“硬的”。馬（參3節）有任性的意志，船隻會遭遇強風，但是這兩種力量都可以用一個較小的裝置來控制。
**舵。**強調這不可少之舵的小。
**掌舵的。**或“舵手”，“司機”。
**意思。**boulomai，“深思熟慮”，“意圖”。雖然舵引導著船隻，但他是受舵手所控制的。同樣，雖然舌頭在一定的意義上指導著全身，但它是受意志所控制的（參雅1:15）。
4.en:
**Ships.** Ships were familiar objects to many of Jame’s readers, for the Roman Empire bordered the Mediterranean Sea.
Great. Ancient ships seemed large to people of that time, though today’s ocean liners far exceed them in size. Paul’s journey to Malta was on large ship for it carried 276 persons, including both crew and passengers (see Acts 27:37). However, any ship is large in comparison with the rudder that controls it.
Fierce. Gr. sklēros, “harsh,” “strong,” “stiff.” The horse (cf. v. 3) possesses its own headstrong will and a ship is the victim of strong winds, but both forces can be controlled by a relatively small device.
Helm. Or, “rudder.” The emphasis is on the smallness of the indispensable rudder.
Governor. Or, “steersman,” or “pilot.”
Listeth. Gr. boulomai, “to will deliberately,” “to purpose.” Although the rudder guides the ship, it is the helmsman who controls the rudder. Similarly, although the tongue may, in a since, give direction to the whole body, it is directed, in turn, by the will (cf. ch. 1:15).

11.zh:
泉源從一個眼裡能發出甜苦兩樣的水嗎？

能……嗎？原文暗示期待否定的回答。
**泉源。**pēgē，“泉”。泉源是水的來源，心也是話語的來源（見箴4:23,24註釋）。雖然泉源是無生命的，但它的湧流卻是受自然律所控制的。所以基督徒的行為也當與他們重生本性的相和諧。使徒以本性上不可能的事來推論荒謬的事，但不幸的是，人類的行為真的很荒謬。
**眼。**opē，“出口”，“裂縫”。
**發出。**直譯是“湧出”。
**甜。**新鮮的。
**苦。**味道不好的。從一口泉眼裡不可能同時湧出甜苦兩樣的水。熟悉巴勒斯坦的人會想到，死海附近的礦泉水與北方黎巴嫩融雪的淡水是不一樣的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督教育原理》第167頁；《證言》卷七第167頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–18節）**。《證言》卷二第178頁。
11.en:
Doth? The Greek implies that a negative answer is expected.
Fountain. Gr. pēgē, “spring.” As the fountain is the source of water, so the heart is the source of words (see on Prov. 4:23, 24), Though a fountain is inanimate, its flow is regulated by the laws of nature. Accordingly, Christian men should act in harmony with the law of their renewed nature. The apostle reasons from what is impossible in nature to what is absurdly, but unfortunately, true in human conduct.
Send forth. Literally, “gush forth.”
Place. Gr. opē, “opening,” “cleft.”
Sweet. That is, fresh.
Bitter. That is, brackish. No spring pours forth fresh and brackish water from the same cleft. Those familiar with Palestine would think of the contrast between the mineral springs near the Dead Sea and the fresh streams of the north, fed by the snows of Lebanon.

12.zh:
我的弟兄們，無花果樹能生橄欖嗎？葡萄樹能結無花果嗎？鹹水裡也不能發出甜水來。

能……嗎？原文暗示期待否定的回答。
**無花果樹。**果樹與泉水都是各從其類的，不可能有其他的結果。雅各在這裡說明咒詛和辱罵的舌頭顯然證明一個人不是真基督徒。他沒有暗示悔改的人不可能再墮入罪中（參2節），但他確實指出真正悔改的人不會再發出非基督化的言論（見10節）。
**葡萄樹。**這個例子像基督所舉過的例子（見太7:16）。雅各主要並不是在善與惡之間進行對比，而是強調樹木結果必須“各從其類”（創1:11,12）。反過來說，果子的性質也一定會證實結果之樹的種類（見太7:20）。雅各在這裡說明真敬拜不可能出自邪惡的心。他的結論特別適合於教師們。
12.en:
Can? The Greek implies that a negative answer is expected.
Fig tree. Fruit trees and springs of water produce according to their respective natures. No other result is expected. James here suggests that cursing and other abuses of the tongue obviously mark a person as not a genuine Christian. He does not imply that a converted person never lapses into sin (cf. v. 2), but he does show that a truly converted person will not make a practice of engaging in un-Christlike speech (see on v. 10).
Vine. The illustrations here used resemble those employed by Christ (see Matt. 7:16). James is not primarily contrasting good with bad, but insists that a tree must produce “after his kind” (Gen. 1:11, 12) and that, conversely, the nature of the fruit inevitably testifies the kind of tree that produced it (see Matt. 7:20).
So. Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) the reading of the last clause of v. 12 as follows: “Neither can salt water produce fresh water.” James here shows that it is impossible for true worship to come from a heart of evil. His conclusions are especially applicable to teachers.

13.zh:
你們中間誰是有智慧有見識的呢？他就當在智慧的溫柔上顯出他的善行來。

**有智慧的。**雅各在這裡所說的是虔誠的生活所需要的智慧（見林前6:5；弗5:15）。
**有見識的。**或“有理解力的”。
**顯出。**真智慧將表現在行為上。一個人所結的果子將顯明他的本性，如12節所強調的。
**善。**kalos，“好的”，“值得表揚的”。
**行。**anastrophē，“生活方式”，“品行”。參弗2:3；見加1:13；提前4:12；來13:7；彼前1:15；見弗4:22註釋。
行為。就是出於信心的行為。
**溫柔。**praütēs（見雅1:21的註釋）。虛假的溫柔只是驕傲和缺乏積極性的表現。真正溫柔智慧的人會以一種溫和而堅定的態度說明自己的信念，實行自己的計劃。溫柔的精神最有利於冷靜的管理和清晰的思維。一個智慧的人在上帝面前是謙卑的。這種屬靈經驗阻止了傲慢和無情地管轄同胞的作法（參雅2:13）。見多識廣不等於有智慧。只有行為“溫柔”才表明受過教育的人真有智慧。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《今日的生活》第111頁；《證言》卷二第544頁；《證言》卷五第175頁。
13.en:
**A wise man.** Rather, “wise.” James is here speaking of wisdom such as is needed for pious living (see 1 Cor. 6:5; Eph. 5:15).
Endued with knowledge. Or, “understanding.”
Shew. Genuine wisdom will be demonstrated in works. The nature of a man will be shown by the fruit he produces, as emphasized in v. 12.
Good. Gr. kalos, “excellent,” “commendable.”
Conversation. Gr. anastrophē, “manner of life,” “conduct.” Compare Eph. 2:3; see Gal. 1:13; 1 Tim. 4:12; Heb. 13:7; 1 Peter 1:15; see on Eph. 4:22.
Works. That is, works of faith.
Meekness. Gr. praütēs, “gentleness” (see on ch. 1:21). False meekness is mere complacency and lack of initiative. The truly meek wise man speaks his convictions and implements his plans in a gentle, though firm, manner. Gentleness of spirit is most conducive to clear thinking as well as to calm administration. A wise man is humble before God, and this spiritual experience becomes a barrier against arrogance and merciless domination of his fellow men (cf. ch. 2:13). A wide grasp of facts alone does not constitute wisdom, for “meekness” in conduct marks the educated man as truly wise.

14.zh:
你們心裡若懷著苦毒的嫉妒和紛爭，就不可自誇，也不可說謊話抵擋真道。

**心。**自私結黨可能在外表上看不出來，但它像泉源裡的苦水一樣（參11節），總有一天會在言行中表現出來。雅各暗示需要認真地省察心靈。
**嫉妒。**zēlos，“熱心”，貶義為“嫉妒”（見約2:17）。其含義取決於所追求的目標。雅各在本節所說的是貶義的嫉妒，因為它是“苦毒的”。這種妒忌與上述的溫柔（雅3:13）形成了鮮明的對照。
**紛爭。**eritheia，“結黨”，“分派”，“利己”。為了促進自己的特殊利益，人會變得非常嫉妒，絲毫不顧別人的意願。基督徒最需要有“智慧的溫柔”。
**不可自誇。**基督徒不要誇耀個人的成就或技能。結黨的人通常以自吹自擂來吸引支持者。這樣的自誇缺乏真智慧。服務才是聲望唯一可靠的基礎。
**真道。**就是福音真理。一個自稱有智慧的人不要因自己缺乏真理的精神而背叛真理。基督教的真理表現在生活方式上。真理的理論只有在表顯真理的化身──基督的品行時才有價值（見約壹2:6註釋；見約14:6；《教會證言》卷三第59頁）
**懷愛倫註釋（14–18節）**。《證言》卷五第225頁。
14.en:
**Envying.** Gr. zēlos, “zeal,” in a bad sense, “jealousy” (see on John 2:17). The morality of the “zeal” depends upon the objective pursued. Here James speaks of evil zeal, for it is “bitter.” Such zeal stands in sharp contrast with the meekness earlier described (James 3:13).
Strife. Gr. eritheia, “partisanship,” “a factious spirit,” “self-interest.” Men may become bitterly zealous over promoting their special interests and show little regard for the desires of others. The “meekness of wisdom” is the prime requisite for the Christian.
Hearts. The factious self-interest may be hidden from outward appearance, but it is like the bitter water in a fountain (cf. v. 11)—one day it will flow forth in word or deed. James implies that a careful heart examination is always necessary.
Glory not. Or, “stop boasting.” Christians are not to boast of personal achievements or skills. Those with a partisan spirit usually seek to attract supporters by self-assertion. Such boasting reveals a lack of genuine wisdom. Service is the only sound basis for popularity.
Truth. That is, the truth of the gospel. One who professes to be wise should not betray the truth he teaches by his own lack of the spirit of truth. Christian truth consists in a way of life. The theory of the truth is worth while only when it finds expression in conduct that reveals Christ, the embodiment of truth (see on 1 John 2:6; see John 14:6; 3T 59)

15.zh:
這樣的智慧不是從上頭來的，乃是屬地的，屬情慾的，屬鬼魔的。

**這樣的智慧。**指缺乏溫柔的精神、違背真理之人的智慧（見13節註釋）。雅各承認有兩種智慧，就像他所說有兩種信心一樣（見雅2:17註釋）。這樣的智慧和死的信心一樣，都只是名義上的。它實際上只是精明，邏輯能力和善於論辯，全都用於自己的利益。
**不是從上頭來的。**領導工作中錯用的學問和技術並不是從上帝來的。祂是真智慧的創始者（見《歷代願望》219頁；見雅1:5註釋）。上帝並不賜下智慧幫助那些苦苦競爭和自私自利的人（見雅3:14註釋）。
**屬地的。**這種所謂的智慧源於屬世的原則和動機，併為屬世的目的服務。它只看到今生。
**屬情慾的。**psuchikos，“不屬靈的”（見林前15:44註釋）。屬世的智慧尋求滿足人本性的慾望和嗜好。
**屬鬼魔的。**或“像魔鬼的”。參雅2:19。自稱的智慧不僅缺乏“從上面來的”智慧的特徵，而且肯定帶有魔鬼的特徵。鬼魔的首領路錫甫曾不滿足於上帝賜給他的智慧（見結28:17）。這種嫉妒的精神最終導致他“苦毒的嫉妒紛爭”（參雅3:14）。有人認為“屬地的”，“屬情慾的”和“屬鬼魔的”是指人類的三個屬靈仇敵——世界，肉體和魔鬼。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第474，554頁；《成聖的人生》第30頁；《救贖的故事》第395頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–18節）**。《證言》卷八第242頁。
15.en:
**This wisdom.** That is, the wisdom of those who betray the truth by a spirit void of meekness (see on v. 13). James recognizes two kinds of wisdom, as he has recognized two kinds of faith (see on ch. 2:17). As with a deadfaith, this kind of wisdom is such in name only. In fact, it is shrewdness, logical skill, and subtle arguments, all employed in self-interest.
Not from above. Misdirected learning and skill in leadership are not from God, who is the author of true wisdom (see DA 219; see on ch. 1:5). God does not give wisdom to aid those who are concerned with bitter wrangling and self-interest (see on ch. 3:14).
Earthly. This professed wisdom springs from earthly principles and motives and is intent upon serving earthly purposes. It has only this present life in view.
Sensual. Gr. psuchikos, “unspiritual” (see on 1 Cor. 15:44). Earthly wisdom seeks to satisfy the desires and propensities that spring from within the natural man.
Devilish. Or, “demonlike.” Compare ch. 2:19. Professed wisdom not only lacks the characteristics of the wisdom that is “from above,” but contains positive elements that are characteristic of demons. Lucifer, now the chief of demons, was not satisfied with the wisdom God had bestowed upon him (see Eze. 28:17). Eventually this envious spirit led him to “bitter envying and strife” (cf. James 3:14). Some see in the three expressions “earthly,” “sensual,” and “devilish” the three spiritual foes of man—the world, the flesh, and the devil.
Envying and strife See on v. 14.
Confusion. Gr. akatastasia, “state of disorder,” “restlessness.” Compare chs. 1:8; 3:8. The result of self-interest in a home or in a church is always a state of instability that leads to unhappiness and confusion. Thus, wisdom that is not “from above” will eventually reveal its true nature by its fruit.
Evil. Gr. phaulos, “worthless,” “good for nothing.” A program born in self-interest and promoted by a spirit of ruthless domination will eventually fail because of its own inherent weaknesses. Sin and self-interest never produce harmony.

16.zh:
在何處有嫉妒、紛爭，就在何處有擾亂和各樣的壞事。

**嫉妒紛爭。**見14節註釋。
**擾亂。**akatastasia，“混亂”，“不安寧”。參雅1:8；3:8。在家庭或教會中，自私自利的結果總是導致不幸和混亂的不穩定局面。所以不是“從上面來的”智慧最終會藉著果實暴露出其真面目。
**壞事。**phaulos，“沒有價值的”。出於自私自利，並以無情統治的精神為動機的計劃，最終會因為其本身的弱點而失敗。罪與自私永遠不會產生和諧。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第385頁。

26.en:
**Spirit.** Or, “breath.” The apostle closes his argument with an irrefutable fact that he invites his opponents to consider—there is not life in the body when the breath is absent (see on Gen. 2:7).
Faith. That is, so-called faith, because apart from works genuine faith does not exist. Intellectual assent, creedal conviction, may exist without good works, but not living faith, which cooperates with God’s plan for man’s restoration.
Dead. There was nothing dead about either Abraham’s or Rahab’s faith or that of any of the other heroes of faith honored in Heb. 11. By faith they obeyed. Church members in name only, without personal witness that reflects the ministry of Christ on their behalf, are, as it were, mere corpses.
26.zh:
身體沒有靈魂是死的，信心沒有行為也是死的。

**靈魂。**或“呼吸”。使徒用一個無可辯駁的事實來結束他的論證。他請反對他的人注意：沒有呼吸，人體就沒有生命（見創2:7註釋）。
**信心。**這是所謂的信，因為沒有行為就不存在真正的信心。理智上贊成，教義的相信，可以在沒有好行為的情況下存在，但這不是活的信心，不能配合上帝恢復人類的計劃。
**死的。**亞伯拉罕，喇合，以及《希伯來書》11章所表揚的其他任何一位信心的英雄，他們的信心都不是死的。他們因信而順從。那些名義上的信徒，沒有反映基督為他們服務的個人見證，就像是行屍走肉一般。

9.en:
**Respect.** See on v. 3.
Sin. By showing deference to the “rich,” Christians could conceivably think that they were fulfilling the law of love. But this very law shows that they are sinning by their practice of exhibiting partiality in their dealings with people.
Convinced. Gr. elegchō, “to convict [with proof of guilt],” “to expose” (see on John 16:8).
Law. The law is the perfect standard of righteousness by which the deeds of men are evaluated (see on Rom. 3:20; James 1:25).
Transgressors. Gr. parabatai, literally, “those who deviate from the [true] way.”
9.zh:
但你們若按外貌待人，便是犯罪，被律法定為犯法的。

**按外貌待人。**見第3節註釋。
**犯。**elegchō，“認定（犯罪的證據）”，“暴露”（見約16:8註釋）。
**罪。**基督徒對“富足人”表示偏愛，可能以為自己是在實行愛的律法。但是這個律法顯明他們犯了偏待人的罪。
**律法。**律法是衡量人類行為的公義的完全標準（見羅3:20；雅1:25註釋）。
**犯法的。**parabatai，直譯是是“離開（正）路的人”。

18.en:
**Yea.** Gr. alla, “but.” James here presents two hypothetical persons engaged in an argument, one speaker being “thou” and the other “I.” The former, apparently a Christian, claims to be saved by faith alone, and the latter, apparently a Jew, perhaps a Christian Jew, by his own works. James does not exactly share either point of view, but addresses his own challenge (in the latter part of the verse) to the man who argues for faith alone.
Shew. Gr. deiknumi, “to demonstrate,” “to give proof.” James, as it were, now enters the argument and exposes the fallacy of thinking that faith can exist apart from works.
Without. To show faith apart from works is an impossible task because faith, being a principle, an attitude of the mind, will always reveal its nature in outward behavior. But one who exhibits an absence of good works thereby also demonstrates a lack of genuine faith.
I will shew. Genuine faith will find expression in unselfish deeds, for it begets a desire to serve men. Thus it was Christ and thus it will be with all who follow His example.
18.zh:
必有人說：你有信心，我有行為；你將你沒有行為的信心指給我看，我便藉著我的行為，將我的信心指給你看。

**必。**alla，“但是”。雅各在這裡假設兩個正在辯論的人：“你”和“我”。“你”顯然指一個聲稱單靠信心得救的基督徒；“我”顯然是依靠自己行為的猶太人，或許是一個猶太籍的基督徒。雅各沒有偏袒任何一方，而只是向主張單靠信心的人提出問題（本節後半部分）。
**沒有。**沒有行為的信心是不可能存在，因為信心是一種原則和思想態度，總會在外表的行為上表現出它的性質。所以沒有好行為的人也就沒有真正的信心。
**指給。**deiknumi，“說明”，“證明”。雅各現在似乎捲入了爭論，指出信心能離開行為而存在的謬誤。
**指給你看。**真正的信心會表現在無私的行為中，因為它會產生一種為人服務的願望。基督是這樣，效法祂榜樣的人也是這樣。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》第41頁；《基督教育原理》第337頁；《先祖與先知》第279頁；《證言》卷一第123，132頁；《證言》卷四第308，596頁；《證言》卷五第537頁。

10.en:
**Keep.** Gr. tēreō, “to guard,” “to attend to carefully.” James here sets forth the example of a church member who supposedly keeps the whole law, save for one point. He does not say that such an example actually exists.
Offend. Gr. ptaiō, “to stumble,” “to fail in one’s duty.”
Point. The law is not a mere collection of isolated precepts; it is a perfect harmonious transcript of the divine will. All the precepts are manifestations of love at work, either to God or to our fellow men. To select that part of the law that is convenient and to ignore the claims of the rest, even if in only one detail, reveals a desire to do our own will and not God’s. The unity of love is broken and the basis sin of selfish willfulness appears.
Guilty of all. Lawbreaking, whether civil or religious, need not be a violation of all the laws—one violation is enough. The basic question if loyalty to authority is the primary problem, and one violation is sufficient to show the disposition of the heart. it at one point is to violate love as such, the whole of it” Columbus, Ohio, 1946,
As a chain is snapped by the failure of its weakest link, as one note may spoil the whole harmony, as one wounded part injures the entire body, or as leprosy in any part causes the whole man to be called leprous, so the breaking of one commandment spoils the completeness and harmony of the whole law for the transgressor.
10.zh:
因為凡遵守全律法的，只在一條上跌倒，他就是犯了眾條。

**遵守。**tēreō，“看守”，“小心照看”。雅各在這裡舉例說，假定有一位信徒認為自己除了一條之外，已經遵守了全部的律法。他沒有說這樣事情真實存在。
**一條。**律法不只訓令的彙編；它是上帝旨意的完美副本。所有的訓令都是愛上帝或愛同胞的具體表現。選擇一部分方便的律法而忽略其餘的要求，即使是一個細節，也表明我們要隨從自己的意願，而不是隨從上帝的旨意。愛的統一既遭到破壞，自私剛愎的罪惡就出現了。
**跌倒。**ptaiō，或“未能履行職責”。
**犯了眾條。**不論是違犯國家法律還是宗教法律，都不需要違犯全部。違犯一條就夠了。主要的問題是服從什麼權威。犯一條就足以表明其思想傾向了。
“鏡子只須打破一點就算是破碎的。律法不是十根針，打倒了一根還有九根立著。律法是一個整體；維繫它的就是愛；違犯了一條就是違反其愛的核心”（倫斯基《希伯來書和雅各書註釋》，572頁）。
鏈條可以在最薄弱的環節斷裂，就像一個音符會破壞整體的和諧，一個傷處會危及全身，一個部位會使整個人被稱為麻瘋病人，違犯一條誡命，對於違犯的人而言，就是破壞了整部律法的完全與和諧。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《復臨信徒家庭》第327頁；《歷代願望》第763頁；《佈道論》第372頁；《基督教育原理》第118頁；《善惡之爭》第582頁；《福山寶訓》第51頁；《證言》卷一第532頁；《證言》卷三第524頁；《證言》卷四第55，253頁。

17.en:
**Faith.** Literally, “the faith,” that is, the “faith” without “works” of v. 14. Such a faith is merely an intellectual conviction that certain doctrines are true. The mind is convinced because of the overwhelming evidence from God’s Word, but the heart remains cold and unconverted.
Not works. As good wishes for the poor and needy can be shown to be genuine by works only, so faith cannot be proved genuine without works. Faith without the fruit of Christian works is faith in name only, without the living principle controlling the actions of the heart (cf. Rom. 2:13; 1 Cor. 13).
Dead. Like a corpse, faith without works may retain an outward resemblance to its living counterpart, but it is lifeless. As a dead vine bears no fruit, dead faith produces no consistent pattern of Christian deeds. Both are worthless.
Being alone. James is not comparing faith with works, but a genuine faith with a dead faith. The dead faith believes in God, but it will prove useless in that this mental conviction has not made Christian service a life habit. In addition to being worthless in this life, this dead faith cannot save its owner (see on v. 14).
17.zh:
這樣，信心若沒有行為就是死的。

**若。**雅各不是在比較信心與行為，而是在比較真信心與死信心。死的信心相信上帝，但沒有用處，因為這種頭腦上的信念未能使基督徒的服務成為生活的習慣。這種死的信心不但在今生沒有價值，而且也救不了人（見14節）
**信心。**就是14節沒有“行為”的“信心”。這種信心只是頭腦上確信某些教義是對的。他們相信是因為聖經無法抗拒的證據，但內心依然冷淡而沒有改變。
**沒有行為。**對於貧乏之人的善意只能用行動來證實。所以沒有行為的信心就不能證明是真的。沒有基督徒行為果子的信心只是名義上的信心，因為沒有活潑的原則來控制心靈的活動（參羅2:13；林前13）。
**死的。**沒有行為的信心像屍體一樣，在外表看是活的，實際上卻是無生命的。正如死葡萄藤結不出葡萄，死的信心也結不出基督徒始終不渝的品行。它們都是沒有價值的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》第29頁；《先祖與先知》第73，154頁；《拾級就主》第61頁；《證言》卷一第192，620，705頁；《證言》卷二第159，167，236，645，663頁；《證言》卷三第249，393頁；《證言》卷四第58，228頁；《論福利工作》第316頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–19節）**。《證言》卷二第657頁。

22.en:
Seest thou? Or, “thou seest.” The Greek may be read as a simple statement, and probably should be here. The illustration of the experience of Abraham is clear for all to comprehend.
Faith. Literally, “the faith,” that is, the faith that prompted Abraham to offer Isaac.
Wrought with. Gr. sunergeō, “to work together,” “to cooperate with.” This verse marks the logical climax of the argument concerning the relationship of faith to works. James is not primarily contending for the recognition of works but for the complete union of genuine faith and Christians deeds. No man can willingly face problems and hazards unless he possesses the inner girding of a steadfast faith. True faith helps men to do great works.
By works. See on v. 21. The “works” of Abraham here referred to consisted of obedience to God’s commands, not of the performance of a routine of works prescribed by human authority.
Perfect. Gr. teleioō, “to bring [something], to its goal,” “to complete” (see on Matt. 5:48; Luke 13:32). Faith and works cannot be separated in a genuine Christian life. when the test came to Abraham his works provided proof that his faith was genuine.
Fulfilled. That is, fully realized (cf. Gen. 15:6; see on Matt. 5:17). Before the birth of Isaac God declared that Abraham would have many descendants (see on Gen. 15:1–5). This prophecy depended upon the birth of a son and the perpetuation of the family line. Abraham believed God’s promise would come true even though he was still childless in his old age (see on Gen. 15:6). Now, many years later, God called for an act that would apparently thwart the original promise to make Abraham a great nation. But Abraham still trusted the wisdom of God and obeyed.
Believed. See on Gen. 15:6.
Imputed. Gr. logizomai, “to reckon,” “to count” (see on Rom. 4:3). Abraham was declared righteous because he trusted God’s word and joyfully accepted the promise of a Redeemer (see on Gal. 3:6). The crowning evidence that he trusted God was revealed in his willingness to slay Isaac at God’s command-an act that apparently would have nullified God’s own promises. This supreme ordeal vindicated God’s declaration of the patriarch’s worthiness.
Friend of God. See 2 Chron. 20:7. This title was commonly applied to Abraham by the Jews, and is current among Arabs today. The transparent genuineness of Abraham’s trust in God is an example all should aspire to emulate.
22.zh:
可見信心是與他的行為並行，而且信心因著行為才得成全。

**可見。**有文本為疑問句。但這裡用陳述句比較合理。用亞伯拉罕的經驗為例證是人人都能夠明白的。
**信心。**指促使亞伯拉罕獻上以撒的信心。
**並行。**sunergeō，“同工”，“合作。”本節是信心與行為關係的最高論點。雅各所爭取的，不是行為得到承認，而是真信心與基督徒行為的完全統一。如果裡面沒有堅定的信心，任何人都不可能甘心面對困難和危險。真信心幫助人們作出偉大之舉。
**因著行為。**見21節註釋。這裡說亞伯拉罕的“行為”就是順從上帝的命令，而不是履行人間的權威所規定的日常工作。
**成全。**teleioō，“達到目標”，“完成”（見太5:48；路13:32註釋）。在真基督徒的生活中，信心與行為是分不開的。當考驗臨到亞伯拉罕時，他的行為證明了他信心的真實性。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》第263頁；《先祖與先知》第73頁；《救贖的故事》第289頁；《證言》卷二第689頁；《證言》卷三第393頁；見路17:10；弗2:8.9懷愛倫註釋。

12.en:
**Speak.** In summation, the apostle exhorts his fellow church members to strive for a daily practice of speaking and doing that is conformable to God’s law. James’s assertion that men are responsible for their words and deeds is characteristic of him, and is another allusion to the teachings of Christ (see Matt. 12:36, 37).
Judged. The life record of every man will one day be reviewed by God (see on Acts 17:31; 2 Cor. 5:10).
Law of liberty. See on James 1:25. In addition to the Decalogue, the other “words” which Jesus spoke will also finally judge men (see on John 12:48). “Sin can triumph only by enfeebling the mind, and destroying the liberty of the soul. Subjection to God is restoration to one’s self,—to the true glory and dignity of man. The divine law, to which we are brought into subjection, is ‘the law of liberty’” (DA 466). See Mishnah Aboth 6.2.
12.zh:
你們既然要按使人自由的律法受審判，就該照這律法說話行事。

**使人自由的律法。**見雅1:25註釋。除了十誡之外，耶穌說的其它的“話”最終也要審判人（見約12:48註釋）。“只有藉著削弱人的意志，摧毀他心靈的自由，罪才能取得勝利。人歸順上帝，就是自我恢復——恢復人類真正的榮耀和尊嚴。我們所要順服的上帝律法，就是‘使人自由的律法’。”（《歷代願望》466頁）。見《密西拿》Aboth 6.2.
**說話。**使徒在總結中勸勉同道爭取每天的言行都符合與帝的律法。雅各認為：人需要對自己的言行負責。這裡又一次引用了基督的教訓（見太12:36,37）。
**受審判。**每個人的生活記錄有朝一日都要受到上帝的審查（見徒17:31；林後5:10註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第466頁；《善惡之爭》第482頁。

24.en:
**Ye see.** Using Abraham as an example of the inseparability of faith and works, James now draws his conclusion to the argument of vs. 14–23.
By works. No man who chooses to be increasingly like Christ will live a life barren of good works.
Is justified. James does not deny that a man is declared righteous by faith, for the quotation he has just given from Gen. 15:6 is evidence of this belief. However, he does deny that a mere profession of faith alone can justify a man. Good works accompany faith and prove the validity of the faith by which a man is justified. If there are no “works,” it is evident that genuine faith does not exist (see on James 2:17, 20).
Only. Or, “alone.” The apostle continues to stress the inseparability of faith and works (see on v. 22). He, of course, is not discussing the problem of “works of the law” in the sense of the ritual requirements of Judaism (see on Rom. 3:28).
24.zh:
這樣看來，人稱義是因著行為，不是單因著信。

**這樣看來。**雅各用亞伯拉罕作為信心與行為不可分開的例子，總結他14-23的論述。
**稱義。**雅各並不否認人是因信稱義的，因為他上面所引的創15:6就是這種信心的證據。但他確實否認單憑自稱有信心就能使人稱義。善行伴隨著信心，證明使人稱義之信心的有效性。如果沒有“行為”，就證明人沒有真正的信心（見雅2:17,20）。
**因著行為。**選擇越來越像基督的人絕不會過一種沒有好行為的生活。
**單。**使徒繼續強調信心與行為不可分割（見22節註釋）。當然他並不是從猶太教儀文要求的意義上討論“遵行律法”的問題（見羅3:28註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第472頁；《證言》卷三第526頁。

25.en:
**Likewise.** James cites another well-known OTincident to illustrate the principle of faith demonstrated by good works. The lesson is parallel with that drawn from Abraham’s experience, though the supreme act of faith in each case differed much from the other.
Rahab. See on Joshua 2:1; Heb. 11:31. Abraham was noted for piety; Rahab for immorality. Abraham believed for many years before the offering up of Isaac; Rahab possessed a young faith. But both proved their faith by their utter disregard for personal security and by casting their lot with God’s program. James shows that the most venerated of the faithful and the most despised of the Gentiles alike find justification through a faith that works.
Justified. See on v. 21. Rahab cast her lot with the people of God and demonstrated her faith in Israel’s God by jeopardizing her life to save the spies. James implies that if she he had professed faith in the God of Israel and yet had not hidden the spies, her faith would have been barren and dead.
25.zh:
妓女喇合接待使者，又放他們從別的路上出去，不也是一樣因行為稱義嗎？

**喇合。**見書2:1；來11:31註釋。亞伯拉罕以虔誠著稱；喇合則以敗壞而聞名。亞伯拉罕在獻以撒以前已經信了多年；喇合只是初信者。但是他們都通過不顧個人安危服從上帝的計劃而證明了他們的信心。雅各說明最受人尊敬的忠心者和最遭人藐視的外邦人都是因著有行為的信心而稱義的。
**一樣。**雅各引用另一個著名的《舊約》事例，來說明善行證明信心的原理。這個教訓與亞伯拉罕經驗的教訓是一樣的，但是其信心的最高表現則是不同的。
**稱義。**見21節註釋。喇合把自己的命運同上帝的子民聯繫在一起，冒著生命的危險搭救兩位探子，表明她相信以色列的上帝。雅各暗示如果她自稱相信以色列上帝，卻沒有掩護兩個探子，她的信心就是沒有結果的，是死的信心。

5.en:
**Hearken.** As it were, James here brings these self-constituted judges to trial (v. 4).
Brethren. See on chs. 1:2; 2:1.
Chosen. Gr. eklegomai (see on Rom. 8:33). The form of the Greek word here used emphasizes that God chooses men for Himself. That is, He chooses men who make it a life habit to contemplate, and to trust in, Jesus (see on John 6:40). God will take unto Himself only those who genuinely desire to be like Him. Paul also uses eklegomai to describe God’s choice of the “base things of the world” in the formation of the Christian church (see on 1 Cor. 1:26–28).
Poor of this world. That is, poor in the estimation of this world. Because the “world” (see on ch. 1:27) judges a man’s worth on the basis of his material possessions, the poor are often despised by those more fortunate. However, Christ has pronounced a blessing on them, teaching that His kingdom will be made up largely of the poor (see on Luke 6:20–25). Men are not called because they are poor but because they are willing to give wholehearted loyalty to Jesus Christ and to trust Him completely (see on Matt. 6:33). The possessions of the rich man often become a substitute for trust in God. Consequently, complete confidence in Christ may not seem so needful to the rich man as it does to the poor man.
Rich in faith. That is, rich in the exercise of faith. The same man may be poor in the eyes of the world but rich in the sight of God.
Heirs of the kingdom. James is here speaking of the future kingdom of glory, the plan for which was laid prior to the entrance of sin into our world (see Dan. 7:27; see on Matt. 25:34). Christians are not only heirs but “joint-heirs” with Jesus, and obtain all the privileges that such an honor imparts (see on Rom. 8:17). This “kingdom” may be compared with the “crown of life” (James 1:12), which also is given “to them that love him.”
5.zh:
我親愛的弟兄們，請聽，神豈不是揀選了世上的貧窮人，叫他們在信上富足，並承受他所應許給那些愛他之人的國嗎？

**兄弟們。**見雅1:2；2:1註釋。
**請聽。**雅各似乎讓這些自命為判斷別人的人接受審判（4節）。
**揀選。**eklegomai（見羅8:33註釋）。原文強調上帝親自揀選人。祂揀選那些已經養成默想和信靠耶穌生活習慣的人（見約6:40註釋）。上帝只接納那些真正希望像祂的人。保羅也用eklegomai來形容上帝揀選“世上卑賤的”人組成基督的教會（見林前1:26-28註釋）。
**世上的貧窮人。**就是世人視為貧窮的人。因為“世俗”（見雅1:27註釋）是依據人的物質財富判斷其價值的。窮人往往受到富人的藐視。但基督為窮人宣佈了一個福氣，教導說祂的國度將主要由窮人所組成（見路6:20-25註釋）。人蒙召不是因為他們貧窮，而是因為他們願意完全效忠耶穌基督，並全然信靠祂（見太6:33註釋）。富人常以財產來代替對上帝的信靠。結果他們覺得自己不需要像窮人那樣完全信靠基督。
**在信上富足。**就是有信心的豐富經驗。一個人在世人眼中可能是貧窮的，但在上帝眼中卻是富足的。
**承受祂所應許給那些愛祂之人的國。**雅各在本節指的是將來榮耀的國度。這個國度的計劃在罪惡進入我們世界之前就已經制定（見但7:27；見太25:34註釋）。基督徒不止是後嗣，而且是與耶穌“同做後嗣”，並擁有這種尊榮所帶來的一切特權（見羅8:17註釋）。這個“國”可以與應許賜給“那些愛祂之人的”“生命的冠冕”（雅1:12）相比。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《健康勉言》第424頁；《佈道論》第565頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–6節）**。《證言》卷二第160頁。

11.en:
**He.** There is only one Lawgiver (cf. ch. 4:12), the law being the expression of His will (see on Ex. 20:1). Thus His authority is equally revealed in each of the ten precepts spoken by Him on Sinai, and whoever deliberately violates one commandment rebels against the expressed will of God.
Said. Probably a reference to the fact that the Lord spoke the Ten Commandments (see Ex. 20:1; Deut. 5:26).
Do not commit adultery. The apostle cites two of the Ten Commandments as examples, although any other two would have been equally illustrative. The Lord Himself cited these same two commandments in the Sermon on the Mount, where He shows that they may be violated in the heart as well as by an overt act (see Matt. 5:21–28). With this illustration James shows that the keeping of one part of the law does not cancel the violation of another part. No earthly judge will pardon the violation of one law simply because the culprit has kept many other laws. Thus, the church members who excused their deference to the rich as a carrying out of the law of love are reminded that this practice does not cancel their injustices to the poor. The unity of genuine Christian love is shattered.
Transgressor. See on v. 9.
Law. The spirit of the whole law is thus violated and reveals a lack of full commitment to God’s will.
11.zh:
原來那說不可姦淫的，也說不可殺人；你就是不姦淫，卻殺人，仍是成了犯律法的。

**那。**立法者只有一位（參雅4:12）。律法表達了祂的旨意（見出20:1註釋）。祂在西奈山所頒佈十誡的每一條同樣都顯示了祂的權威。凡故意違犯其中一條誡命的，就是悖逆上帝所表達的旨意。
**說。**可能指主頒佈十誡（見出20:1；申5:26）。
**不可姦淫。**使徒以十誡中的兩條為例，雖然其他任何兩條也一樣能說明問題。主自己在登山寶訓中曾引用過與這兩條誡命，說明它們既可能公然遭到違犯，也可能在心裡犯下（見太5:21-28）。雅各用這個例子說明，遵守部分律法並不抵消對另一部分的違背。地上沒有法官會只因犯人遵守了其他許多法律就寬恕他違犯一條法律。雅各提醒那些以為對富人偏心就是實行了愛的律法的信徒，這樣作並不能抵消他們對窮人的虧待，因為它破壞了真基督徒愛的合一。
**犯律法的。**見第9節註釋。
**律法。**整部律法的精神就這樣遭到了破壞，表明人不願意完全順服上帝的旨意。

8.en:
**If.** Literally, “if indeed.”
Fulfil. Gr. teleō, “to bring to completion,” “to perform perfectly.” Teleō is stronger than tēreō (v. 10). Compare plēroō “fulfill,” in Matt. 5:18, which is used in the sense of “fill full.”
Royal. Gr. basilikos, “belonging to a king,” hence, “chief,” “supreme.” “Royal law” may thus mean either a law given by a king, here the King of heaven, or a supreme law. The law of love is the supreme principle upon which all other sacred law hangs. This “royal law,” the Decalogue, which is also called the “perfect law” (see on James 1:25; cf. GC 466), is based on this principle.
Scripture. Gr. graphē, literally, “writing.” The rule of Christian practice is settled by the Scriptures. James, in common with other NT writers, employed the term graphē to denote the OT (see on 2 Tim. 3:16). The precept to “love thy neighbour as thyself” first appears in Lev. 19:18, and is endorsed and strengthened by the teachings of Christ (see on Matt 5:43; 19:16–19; 22:37–40; Luke 10:27–29; John 13:34).
Ye do well. The divine approbation rests on the church member who lives out this law of love perfectly in his daily life. But this law applies to the poor as well as to the rich, for both are “neighbours” and without partiality should be considered as equals. Loving only the “rich” as “thyself” is not fulfilling the law.
8.zh:
經上記著說：要愛人如己。你們若全守這至尊的律法，才是好的。

**經上。**graphē，直譯是“著作”。基督徒的行為準則是聖經所決定的。雅各和其他《新約》作者一樣，用graphē指《舊約》（提後3:16）。“愛人如己”的命令最早出現在利19:18中，併為基督的教訓所認可和強調（見太5:43；19:16-19；22:37-40；路10:27-29；約13:34註釋）。
**若。**直譯為“如果真是”。
**全守。**teleō，“完成”，“完全履行”。Teleō比tēreō（10節）要強。參太5:18 plēroō表示“成全”。
**至尊的。**basilikos，“屬於國王的”，故有“主要的”，“最高的”。本節“至尊的律法”可以指國王的律法，在這裡是天上的君王所頒佈的，也可以指至高的律法。愛的律法是維繫其他所有神聖律法的最高原則。這“至尊的律法”，即十誡，又稱“全備的律法”（見雅1:25註釋；參《善惡之爭》466頁），就是基於這個原則。
**才是好的。**上帝悅納在日常生活中完全遵行這愛之律法的信徒。但這律法既用於富人，也適用於窮人身上，因為他們都是“鄰舍”，不應偏愛，要一視同仁。只愛“富人”如“己”並不成全律法。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第466頁。

20.en:
**Wilt.** Gr. thelō, “to be determined,” “to desire.” The clause may be translated “do you desire to know?” James appeals to the intellect, for often the real obstacle to the reception of truth is willful ignorance.
Know. Gr. ginōskō, “to understand appreciatively.”
Vain. Gr. kenos, “empty of content,” “deficient” (see on 1 Cor. 15:14). A dead faith is an empty faith because it will save no one. James, in solemn warning, pleads with those church members who have a faith no more effective than that possessed by demons.
Without. Gr. chōris, “apart from” (cf. v. 18). The idea is not that works cause faith to live, but that a living faith produces living works.
Dead. Important textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 10) for the reading “unproductive,” “barren,” “ineffective.” Regardless of which reading is accepted, the meaning is clear—a mere profession of faith is profitless (see on vs. 14, 16) both to its owner and to those in need.
20.zh:
虛浮的人哪，你願意知道沒有行為的信心是死的嗎？

**虛浮。**kenos，“空洞”，“枉然”（見林前15:14註釋）。死的信心是空洞的信心，因為它救不了人。雅各嚴肅地警告那些信心不比鬼魔的信心更為有效的信徒。
**願意。**thelō，或“決心”。雅各提出了理智，因為接受真理的真正障礙往往是故作不知。
**知道。**ginōskō，“理解”。
**沒有。**Chōris。不是說行為產生活的信心，而是說活的信心產生活的行為。
**死的。**有文本為“沒有出產的”，“不能生育的”，“無效的”。不管怎麼解讀，意思都是很清楚的：單說有信心對於表白的人和需要的人是沒有益處的（見14,16節）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《給管家的勉言》第29頁；《給傳道人的證言》第443頁；《證言》卷四第250，527頁；《證言》卷六第112頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（20–22節）**。《善惡之爭》第472頁。

1.zh:
我的弟兄們，你們信奉我們榮耀的主耶穌基督，便不可按著外貌待人。

**我的弟兄們。**見雅1:2註釋。這個通用的稱呼特別恰當，因為在這裡強調平等的原則。信徒如果保守自己“不沾染世俗”（雅1:27），就會小心避免因貧富而在同道之間產生歧視。
**信奉我們的主。**原文也可理解為“我們主的信心”。但據上下文應該是指“信奉我們的主”（見可11:22；弗3:12註釋）。
**榮耀。**（參林前2:8）。我們的主耶穌擁有神性的一切特權（見本註釋卷五919頁）。祂是“榮耀的王”（詩24:7）。按正確的觀點來看，連最富足的人在分享“榮耀”之主產業的聖徒面前也是貧窮的（見羅8:17註釋）。
**便不可。**上下文暗示教會中有人偏愛“富足人”。所以使徒的勸勉直接針對當地教會的問題。
**按著外貌待人。**prosōpolēpsiai，“偏待人”（見羅2:11註釋）。信徒在“保守自己不沾染世俗”（雅1:27）時應該小心，免得把財富和世俗的地位作為擔任教會職務的資格，以代替必要的屬靈恩賜。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–26節）**。《給傳道人的證言》第125頁。
1.en:
**My brethren.** See on ch. 1:2. This common phrase is especially suitable because of the stress here placed on the principle of equality. If church members keep themselves “unspotted from the world” (ch. 1:27), they will carefully avoid discriminating between fellow believers because of wealth or poverty.
Have not. The context suggests that there had been favoritism in the church toward the “rich.” The apostle’s counsel was therefore directed to an immediate problem in local churches.
Faith of our Lord. The Greek may mean either “our Lord’s faith” or “faith in our Lord.” Here, the context implies that the latter is intended (see on Mark 11:22; Eph. 3:12).
Glory. Literally, “the glory” (cf. 1 Cor. 2:8). Our Lord Jesus possesses all the prerogatives of Deity (see Vol. V, p. 919). He is the “King of glory” (Ps. 24:7). In proper perspective, even the richest of men is poor compared with the saint who shares the inheritance of the Lord of “glory” (see on Rom. 8:17).
Respect of persons. Gr. prosōpolēpsiai, “acts of partiality” (see on Rom. 2:11). In keeping themselves “unspotted from the world” (James 1:27) church members must be careful lest riches and worldly position are made qualifications for church office, in place of the needed spiritual graces.

2.zh:
若有一個人帶著金戒指，穿著華美衣服，進你們的會堂去；又有一個窮人穿著骯髒衣服也進去；

**若有。**雅各現在舉出了一個偏心的具體事例。
**帶著金戒指。**chrusodaktulios。戒指是富人常戴的裝飾。
**華美。**lampros，“閃光”，“美好”，“輝煌”（參路23:11；啟18:14）。
**會堂。**sunagōgē，“會議”，“集會”。這是《新約》中唯一一處用sunagōgē指基督教會。
**骯髒衣服。**就是沒有洗過，沒有好好保管的衣服，與富人的華服形成對照。雅各在這裡似乎是指那些偶然來參加基督徒禮拜的人，而不是指信徒本身。這些來賓訪顯然被人根據財富而區別對待，有人被忽略，有人被尊重。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–5節）**。《證言》卷四第550頁。
2.en:
**For.** James now gives a practical illustration revealing the dangers of partiality.
Assembly. Gr. sunagōgē, “meeting,” “assembly.” This is the only place in the NT where sunagōgē is applied to the Christian church.
With a gold ring. Gr. chrusodaktulios, “with a gold ring [or “rings”] on one’s finger[s].” Rings were common ornaments of the rich.
Goodly. Gr. lampros, “shining,” “magnificent,” “splendid” (cf. Luke 23:11; Rev. 18:14).
Vile raiment. That is, unwashed and poorly kept clothing, in contrast with the elegant clothing of the rich. James here seems to refer to those who casually visit the worship service of Christians rather than to the members themselves. These visitors were evidently being treated according to their riches, one neglected and another honored.

3.zh:
你們就重看那穿華美衣服的人，說：請坐在這好位上；又對那窮人說：你站在那裡，或坐在我腳凳下邊。

重看。有討好之意。
**華美。**lampros（見2節註釋）。
**好位上。**kalōs，有人認為指“舒服”，有人認為指“合意”。不管怎麼理解，都表示尊重和奉承。
**站。**這個窮人沒有受到禮遇，要麼不起眼地站在牆邊，要麼坐在受尊重的信徒或賓客的腳凳之間的地板上。
**下邊。**就是在另一個人的腳凳邊。這個受到禮遇的人既有座位又有腳凳，覺得窮人一屑不顧。
3.en:
**Have respect.** Or, “look upon,” “regard,” with a concern to please.
Gay. Gr. lampros (see on v. 2).
In a good place. Gr. kalōs, which some think here means “comfortably,” and others, “please” (see RSV). Regardless of the reading, the picture is of deference and fawning respect.
Stand. The poor man is given no courteous consideration. The alternative is between standing inconspicuously along the wall or sitting on the floor between the footstools of the presumably more respected members or guests.
Under. That is, beside, another’s footstool. Having a footstool as well as a seat, this favored person treats the poor man as though he were not worth the least attention.

4.zh:
這豈不是你們偏心待人，用惡意斷定人嗎？

**偏心待人。**diakrinō，“區別對待”，“歧視”（參雅1:6註釋）。這種偏心表明人還沒有真正理解主關於謙卑和服侍別人的明訓。信徒們對待貧富的雙重標準，在行動上否認了他們自稱對謙卑之耶穌的效忠（見雅2:1註釋）。他們偏愛富人，表明自己“心懷二意”（雅1:8），在上帝和世界之間搖擺不定。
**斷定。**dialogismois。使徒稱偏心的人為“斷定人的”，因為他們用自己的行動表示了他們的判斷。他們不是用基督的標準來判斷富人和窮人。他們對富人和窮人的判斷是基於一種虛假的價值觀，就是“世俗”的常規（見雅1:27）。在一個真正的基督徒看來，窮人和富人的靈魂是一樣貴重的。髑髏地是偉大的平衡器。
4.en:
**Partial.** Gr. diakrinō, “to make distinctions,” “to differentiate” (cf. on ch. 1:6). Such partiality is really an indication of uncertainty over the plain teachings of the Lord regarding humility and service for others. By this double standard, according to which the rich and the poor are treated so differently, the church members are denying by deed their professed allegiance to the lowly Jesus (see on ch. 2:1). By showing partiality such persons show they are double-minded (ch. 1:8), halting between God and the world.
Thoughts. Gr. dialogismois, “reasonings.” The apostle calls the partial ones “judges” because they have expressed their judgment by their conduct. They judged the rich and the poor by un-Christlike standards. Their judgment in making a distinction between the rich and the poor was based on a false sense of values—the standard usually practiced by the “world” (see ch. 1:27). To a genuine Christian the soul of the poor man is worth as much as the soul of the rich man, Calvary being the great equalizer.

6.zh:
你們反倒羞辱貧窮人。那富足人豈不是欺壓你們，拉你們到公堂去嗎？

**羞辱。**atimazō。本節前半句似乎與第5節的思想更為連貫。上帝對待人的態度與雅各在這裡所提到的信徒完全不同。上帝對所有的人都是一視同仁的，並不依據人屬世的地位身份偏愛任何人。如果上帝像這些信徒那樣判斷和揀選人，就很少有人進入教會，成為“國度後嗣”（參林前1:26）。未信的人把這種歧視的作法看作是基督徒行為的標準。雅各急於要避免的，就是對耶穌基督的這種錯誤表達（見1節）。
**富足人。**就是富人階層，特別是富裕的猶太人（見7節）。早期基督教會所遭受的逼迫是由政治上有勢力的猶太人所策動的，尤其是一貫壓迫窮人的撒都該人（見本註釋卷五52頁；見徒8:1註釋）。
**欺壓。**katadunasteuō。該詞還用來表示魔鬼的壓制（見徒10:38）。信徒們應該按照他們希望別人對他們的待遇來對待別人（見太7:12註釋）。雅各提醒“偏心待人”（4節）的信徒在“富足人”手中所曾遭受的不公正待遇，勸他們避免在教會里也這樣欺壓“窮人”。
**公堂。**kritēria，“法庭”（見林前6:2,4註釋）。不一定指猶太人的法庭，儘管富裕的猶太人經常發動逼迫（見徒16:19；17:6；18:12）。
**懷愛倫註釋（6–7節）**。《使徒行述》第157頁。
6.en:
**Despised.** Gr. atimazō, “to dishonor.” The first sentence of this verse seems to be more closely connected in thought with v. 5. God’s dealings with men are contrasted with those of the church members James here refers to. God treats all men alike, preferring no man on the basis of worldly status. If God had judged and selected men as these church members were doing, how very few of them would then have been in the church and become “heirs of the kingdom” (cf. 1 Cor. 1:26). This practice of discrimination may have appeared to nonchurch members as standard Christian procedure, and it is this false representation of Jesus Christ that James is anxious to avoid (see on v. 1).
Rich. That is, the rich as a class, most particularly the rich Jews (see v. 7). The early persecution of the Christian church was instigated by the politically powerful Jews, notably the Sadducees (see Vol. V, p. 52; see on Acts 8:1), the traditional oppressors of the poor.
Oppress. Gr. katadunasteuō, “to exercise harsh control.” The same Greek word is used to describe the afflictions by Satan (see Acts 10:38). Church members are to treat others as they would wish to be treated (see on Matt. 7:12). James reminds the “partial” (v. 4) church members of the injustices inflicted on them by the “rich,” and thereby urges these members to avoid any similar oppression of the “poor” in their congregation.
Judgment seats. Gr. kritēria, “courts of justice” (see on 1 Cor. 6:2, 4). These courts need not be confined to the Jewish tribunals, although Jewish men of wealth frequently led out in the persecution (see Acts 16:19; 17:6; 18:12).

7.zh:
他們不是褻瀆你們所敬奉（所敬奉：或作被稱）的尊名嗎？

**他們。**原文是強調的，指第6節中的“富足人”。 你們所偏愛的富人，難道沒有褻瀆你們的主嗎？
**褻瀆。**這些褻瀆的富人顯然是指不信的猶太人（見徒13:45）或外邦人，因為基督徒不會“褻瀆”耶穌基督的名。在基督教最初的幾個世紀中，順從基督使信徒的日常生活變得非常艱難。
**你們所敬奉。**這樣的話還出現在徒15:17雅各的發言裡（見摩9:12）。雅各說：鑑於“富足人”（6節）的傲慢行為，富裕的來賓來到教會時，不應受到特別的禮遇。教友們對富人尊敬，應該與對窮人的尊敬和體諒是一樣的。
**尊。**kalos，“美麗的”，“優越的”，“值得尊敬的”。
**名。**無疑指基督的名。門徒就是以祂的名命名（見徒11:26註釋），併為這名受苦的（見徒5:41；彼前4:14-16）。基督的名是“配得尊敬的”，因為它表現出尊榮，並賦予接受者以價值。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《福山寶訓》第107頁；《服務真詮》第491頁。
7.en:
**They.** Emphasis is placed upon this word in the Greek. It refers back to the “rich men” in v. 6. Is it not “they,” these very rich ones who blaspheme your Lord, to whom you are disposed to give preference?
Blaspheme. Obviously these rich blasphemers were either unbelieving Jews (see Acts 13:45) or heathen, for no Christian would “blaspheme” the name of Jesus Christ. It was obedience to Christ that made normal living so difficult in the first few centuries of the Christian Era.
Worthy. Gr. kalos, “beautiful,” “excellent,” “honorable.”
Name. Undoubtedly, the name of Christ, by which the disciples were known (see on Acts 11:26) and for which they suffered (see Acts 5:41; 1 Peter 4:14–16). The name of Christ is “worthy,” or “honorable,” for it reflects honor and imparts worth to those who bear it.
Which ye are called. A similar expression is found in Acts 15:17 in the speech of James (see Amos 9:12). James is saying that in view of these arrogant practices of “rich men” (v. 6) the rich visitor does not deserve the fawning partiality granted him when he visits the church. Church members are to show respect for the rich, but no more than the respect and consideration they show the poor.

13.zh:
因為那不憐憫人的，也要受無憐憫的審判；憐憫原是向審判誇勝。

**審判。**雅各總結他有關偏愛富人的特別忠告。聖經關於“那不憐憫人的，也要受無憐憫的審判”的警告體現了公平的原則。這一點在《舊約》（見撒下22:26,27；箴21:13註釋）和《新約》中（見太5:7；6:15；7:1,18:21-35；25:41-46註釋）都有論述。
**憐憫。**eleos，“同情”，“慈憐”。參太5:7註釋（見《詩篇》36篇補充註釋；見瑪6:8註釋）。
**誇勝。**katakauchaomai，“歡躍”，“誇耀”。 憐憫人的人懷著快樂的信心無畏地面對審判。他知道上帝必憐憫那憐憫人的。上帝在顯示憐憫的時候，並不像撒但所指控的那樣取消公義。十字架證明了這種指控的荒謬（見《歷代願望》761,762頁），並展示了上帝憐憫的輝煌光彩（見詩85:10註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《基督比喻實訓》第178頁；《證言》卷六第282頁。
13.en:
**Judgment.** James concludes his specific counsel concerning favoritism to the rich. The scriptural warning of judgment without mercy to those who fail to practice mercy is an equitable principle, and is set forth in both the OT (see on 2 Sam. 22:26, 27; Prov. 21:13) and the NT (see on Matt. 5:7; 6:15; 7:1, 18:21–35; 25:41–46).
Mercy. Gr. eleos, “compassion,” “pity,” “mercy.” Compare on Matt. 5:7 (see Additional Note on Ps. 36; see on Micah 6:8).
Rejoiceth. Gr. katakauchaomai, “to exult over,” “to boast against.” The merciful man faces the judgment with glad confidence, unafraid. He knows that God will be merciful to those who show mercy. In showing mercy God does not dispense with justice as Satan had charged. The cross proved the falsity of this charge (see DA 761, 762), and revealed the transcendent splendor of the quality of mercy divine (see on Ps. 85:10).

14.zh:
我的弟兄們，若有人說自己有信心，卻沒有行為，有什麼益處呢？這信心能救他嗎？

**弟兄們。**見本章1,5節；見雅1:2註釋。
**信心。**pistis，“確信”，“信靠”（見來11:1註釋）。顯然有信徒提出信心可以不用行為而存在。雅各則主張沒有好“行為”的“信心”是沒有價值的。真正的信心所產生的“行為”會讓別人看到；它的存在並不單在於個人的見證。自稱有“信心”而沒有“行為”的人，就像自以為虔誠卻沒有“清潔的虔誠”行為的人（參雅1:26）。
**行為。**使徒在第1章和第2章中強調了基督徒行為的重要性。他現在直接面對那些自稱有信心卻忽略“清潔的虔誠”本分的人（參雅1:27）。《雅各書》在這裡和保羅的著作一樣（見羅2:6-10註釋），強調信心和行為在真基督徒經驗中的重要性。行為是生命改變的結果。這種行為是因信心的策動而自發的。
有什麼益處呢？即對於永恆的救恩而言。使徒在本節轉到了“清潔的虔誠”（見雅 1:27）的另一面。有些信徒（雅2:1-13）可能以對於愛的律法的誤解而為自己偏愛富人的行為進行辯解。還有些信徒（14-26節）似乎說自己有“信心”而忽略了他們基督徒善行的義務。
**信心能救他嗎。**原文期待否定的回答：“不能！”沒有習慣行善的信心救不了任何人。沒有真信心的善行也是這樣（見羅3:28註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第472頁；《證言》卷二第657，663頁；《證言》卷四第58，250頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–16節）**。《證言》卷二第685頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–17節）**。《證言》卷二第160頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–20節）**。見加5:6懷愛倫註釋。
14.en:
What doth it profit? Literally, “What the profit?” that is, as to eternal salvation. The apostle here turns to another aspect of the practical duties of “pure religion” (see on ch. 1:27). Presumably some church members (ch. 2:1–13) were excusing their deference to the rich on the basis of a perverted use of the law of love. Other church members (vs. 14–26) seemed to excuse themselves from their Christian duty of good works by appealing to their possession of “faith.”
Brethren. See vs. 1, 5; see on ch. 1:2.
Faith. Gr. pistis, “conviction,” “trust” (see on Heb. 11:1). Apparently, the church member in question asserts that faith can exist without works, whereas James contends that “faith” which does not result in good “works” is worthless. Genuine faith is obvious to others from the “works” it produces; its existence does not rest on mere personal testimony. The man who claims “faith” without “works” may be compared with the man who thinks himself to be religious (cf. James 1:26) but fails to manifest the deeds of “pure religion.”
Works. In chs. 1 and 2 the apostle has stressed the importance of Christian deeds. He now directly confronts those who neglect the duties of “pure religion” (cf. ch. 1:27) under the pretense of faith. Here, in common with the writings of Paul (see on Rom. 2:6–10), the epistle of James stresses the necessity of both faith and works in a genuine Christian experience. Works become the conduct of a converted life—deeds that spring forth spontaneously because of the motivation of faith.
Can faith. Literally, “can the faith [that is, faith without works].” The Greek makes clear that James expects a negative answer: “No, of course not.” Faith that does not find expression in habitual good deeds will never save any man, but neither will good deeds without genuine faith (see on Rom. 3:28).
If. James cites a common situation that frequently tests the genuineness of a church member’s faith.
Naked. Gr. gumnos (see on John 21:7). This word frequently describes those who are thinly clad and who face the elements with insufficient protection.
Destitute. Or, “lacking.” This person lacks not merely luxuries but the essentials of life.

15.zh:
若是弟兄或是姊妹，赤身露體，又缺了日用的飲食；

**若。**雅各提到了常用來試驗信徒信心的真實性的一般情況。
**赤身露體。**gumnos（見約21:7註釋）。該詞常指那些衣著單薄，不能禦寒的人。
**缺。**他不僅缺奢侈品，而且缺生活必需品。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–17節）**。《醫療佈道論》第251頁；《論福利工作》第32頁。

16.zh:
你們中間有人對他們說：平平安安地去吧！願你們穿得暖，吃得飽；卻不給他們身體所需用的，這有什麼益處呢？

**你們中間有人。**使徒機智地沒有提到個人，而強調了這種行為的不人道。他心中想到的可能是真實發生的事情。
**平平安安地去吧。**這是猶太人常用的告別辭，但不限於猶太人（見徒16:36）。在這裡是隨便地推卸責任：“去吧，願上帝或某個朋友供給你所需要的。”
**願你們穿得暖吃得飽。**要給寒冷的人衣服穿，給飢餓的人有飯吃，單有信心是不夠的。只宣讀聖經和上帝的命令而不給需要的人提供物質幫的助會成為殘酷的笑柄。原文暗示這些信徒建議由別人來幫助這些人穿得暖。
**所需的。**自命為有“信心”的同道拒不提供生活必需品，儘管這裡暗示他們有條件的滿足這些需要。
**這有什麼益處呢。**這種空洞的信心不能給需要物質幫助的人任何好處。對於失去又一個機會在“最小”的“弟兄”身上幫助基督的信徒自己，也沒有什麼益處（見約壹3:17；見太25:41-45註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷七第291頁。
16.en:
**One of you.** Without personal references the apostle tactfully highlights the inhumanity of such conduct, perhaps with actual occurrences in mind.
Depart in peace. A common form of farewell among the Jews, though not restricted to them (see Acts 16:36). It reveals, here, an offhand shirking of responsibility: “Depart, and may God or some friend provide for your needs.”
Be ye warmed and filled. Something more than faith alone is needed to clothe the shivering body and remove the pangs of hunger. To be given scriptural texts and godly precepts without the material help needed would be cruel mockery. The Greek implies that these church members suggested that someone else was to warm them.
Needful. That which is absolutely necessary for life was denied by fellow church members, who boasted of their “faith,” even though it is implied that they were able to satisfy the needs.
What doth it profit? This empty faith does not profit those who need material help. Nor does it profit the church member who loses another opportunity to help Christ in the person of one of the “least” of His “brethren.” (See 1 John 3:17; see on Matt. 25:41–45).

19.zh:
你信神只有一位，你信的不錯；鬼魔也信，卻是戰驚。

**信。**雅各承認，“死的”信心有可能包含著一種正確的神學觀念。
**上帝一位。**這個道理是一切基督教思想的基礎。信仰一位有位格的全能上帝，將猶太人和早期基督徒與其它宗教的信徒區別開來。
**你信的不錯。**請把雅各的諷刺的話與基督在可7:9所說的話進行對比。神學的正確是重要的，但它只是達到勻稱基督徒生活這一更重要目標的途徑。
**鬼魔。**daimonia，“汙鬼”（見可1:23）。關於鬼魔的起源，見彼後2:4。眾所周知，鬼魔是相信上帝存在的（見可3:11；5:7）。他們頭腦的這種認識是對的，但他們依然是鬼魔。現在沒有人會說，神學上的正確就等於有信心了。救人的信心會改變人的生命。
**戰驚。**phrisso，“毛骨悚然”，“害怕”，“戰慄”。鬼魔相信上帝的存在，但一想到他們在審判中的刑罰就戰慄不已（見太25:41；彼後2:4註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第777頁；《早期著作》第227頁；《拾級就主》第63頁；《證言》卷二第161頁。
19.en:
**Believest.** James concedes that a “dead” faith may accompany a correct theology.
One God. This doctrine underlies all Christian thinking. Belief in one God, omnipotent, personal, distinguished the Jews and early Christians from the followers of other religions.
Thou doest well. Compare James’s irony with that of Christ in Mark 7:9. Theological correctness is essential, but it is only a means to the more important end of a symmetrical Christian life.
Devils. Gr. daimonia, “demons” (see on Mark 1:23). Concerning the origin of demons see 2 Peter 2:4. No one doubts that demons believe in the existence of God (see on Mark 3:11; 5:7). Their belief may be intellectually correct, but they remain demons nevertheless. No one would say now that theological correctness is faith enough. The faith that saves transforms the life.
Tremble. Gr. phrisso, “to bristle,” “to be horrified,” “to shudder.” The demons are so convinced of the existence of God that they shudder at the thought of their punishment in judgment (see on Matt. 25:41; 2 Peter 2:4).

21.zh:
我們的祖宗亞伯拉罕把他兒子以撒獻在壇上，豈不是因行為稱義嗎？

**我們的祖宗亞伯拉罕。**猶太籍和外邦的基督徒都是亞伯拉罕屬靈的後裔（見羅4:10-12；加3:7-9,29註釋）。雅各為了說明他的理由（19節），就引用了聖經的事例。真信徒所追求的，莫過於亞伯拉罕的信心。
這裡不是指上帝第一次在亞伯拉罕的經驗中稱他為義。第一次是發生在以撒出生的好多年前，《羅馬書》第4章曾有所描述。多年以後，上帝藉著要求亞伯拉罕奉獻以撒而考驗了他。亞伯拉罕作出準備奉獻的“行為”，就是拿出了他真正信心的充分憑據。
**獻。**見創22:5-13；來11:17。
**壇。**唯有亞伯拉罕對上帝的信實堅定不移的信心，才能使他作出如此高尚的順從之舉。他的“行為”所表現的信心，像第一次一樣，再次得到了上帝的稱讚（見創22:15-18）。
**因行為。**直譯是“出於行為”。雅各並沒有說單憑“行為”就能稱一個罪人為義。他強調亞伯拉罕的行為證明上帝所宣佈為義的信心的真實性。雅各像保羅一樣（見羅4:1-25；來11:4-39註釋），把信心作為稱義的核心，並通過引用已稱義之人高尚的行為說明其生命力。
**稱義。**dikaioō，（見羅2:13；3:28註釋）。
不是……嗎？原文暗示雅各的讀者會贊同他的言論。
**懷愛倫註釋（21–23節）**。《先祖與先知》第153頁。
21.en:
**Was.** The Greek implies that James’s readers would readily agree with his statement.
Abraham our father. Both Jewish and Gentile Christians are spiritual descendants of Abraham (see on Rom. 4:10–12; Gal. 3:7–9, 29). To his appeal to logic (v. 19) James now adds an appeal to Scripture. Sincere church members could wish for nothing better than a faith like Abraham’s.
Justified. Gr. dikaioō, “to declare righteous” (see on Rom. 2:13; 3:28).
By works. Literally, “out of works.” James does not say that “works” alone will declare a sinner righteous. He is emphasizing that Abraham’s works proved the genuineness of that faith which God had declared righteous. Like Paul (see on Rom. 4:1–25; Heb. 11:4–39), James places faith at the core of justification and illustrates its vitality by citing the worthy deeds of justified men.
When. The occasion referred to is not the first instance in Abraham’s experience when God declared him righteous. That first experience occurred some years before the birth of Isaac, and is described in Rom. 4. Years later God tested Abraham’s faith by calling on him to offer up Isaac. As Abraham engaged in the “works” preparatory to the offering, he gave full proof of the genuineness of his faith.
Offered. See Gen. 22:5–13; Heb. 11:17.
Altar. Only Abraham’s unswerving confidence in the trustworthiness of God can account for this supreme act of obedience. His faith, as evidenced in his “works,” received again, as in the first instance of justification (see Gen. 15:6), the declaration of God’s approval (see Gen. 22:15–18).

23.zh:
這就應驗經上所說：亞伯拉罕信神，這就算為他的義。他又得稱為神的朋友。

**應驗。**就是完全實現（參創15:6；見太5:17註釋）。以撒出生以前，上帝就宣佈亞伯拉罕會有許多子孫（見創15:1-5註釋）。這個預言的實現有賴於一個兒子的出生和家系的延續。亞伯拉罕相信上帝的應許會實現，儘管他年邁無子（見創15:6註釋）。現在時隔多年，上帝要求他所作的事顯然會妨礙使亞伯拉罕成為一個大國的最初應許得以實現。但是亞伯拉罕依然信靠上帝的智慧而順從了。
**信。**見創15:6註釋。
**算為。**logizomai，“視為”（見羅4:3註釋）。亞伯拉罕被稱為義是因為他信靠上帝的話並樂意接受一位救贖主的應許（見加3:6註釋）。他信靠上帝的最高證據表顯在他願意奉上帝的指示殺以撒──一個顯然會使上帝自己的應許失效的舉動。這個嚴酷的考驗證明上帝對先祖的稱讚的是值得的。
**上帝的朋友。**見代下20:7。猶太人一般用這個稱呼指亞伯拉罕；現今在阿拉伯人中也這樣稱呼。亞伯拉罕信靠上帝明顯的真誠是所有的人應當立志效法的榜樣。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先祖與先知》第128，140頁；《證言》卷四第615頁；《證言》卷六第342頁。

0.zh:
**一、卷名**
這封書信和《新約》中其他書信一樣，原來可能沒有卷名。最早的新約抄本之一，西奈抄本里就包括《雅各書》，在書信的開頭沒有卷名，但在結尾處註上“雅各書”。其他早期抄本里均注有“雅各書”。後來的抄本註明其為公普書信，意思是寫給一般教會的，而不是寫給某一個教會和個人的。
尤西比烏稱《雅各書》為七封公普書信的第一封（《教會史》卷二23章）。這七封書信這樣稱呼是因為他們的對象系一般教會，不過這個稱呼並不完全適合於《約翰貳書》和《約翰叄書》，因為這是個人信函。在所有的早期聖經抄本中，從《雅各書》到《猶大書》這七封信是列在《使徒行傳》之後、保羅的書信之前的。公普書信在我們聖經裡的順序是與主要抄本中的順序一致的。
**二、作者**
沒有充分的證據可以確認《雅各書》的作者身份。新約裡有好多人叫雅各，這是猶太人中很普遍的一個名字，單從十二使徒的名單來看，就可以知道這個名字使用者之多（太10:2,3；可3:16-19；路6:14-16）。使徒中有一位是西庇太的兒子，約翰的兄弟雅各。另一個雅各是亞勒腓的兒子，還有一個雅各是十二使徒之一猶大的父親。
可以推定，《雅各書》的作者是聖經裡所提到的某一個雅各，而不是另一個人們所毫不熟悉的雅各。從雅1:1序言的語氣看來，作者似乎是受信人十分熟悉的人物，說話帶有大家所公認的權威口氣。
根據福音書的記載，十二位使徒與主的關係都很密切。但在兩個雅各中，西庇太的兒子似乎更傑出一些。只有極少數作家認為該信為他所寫，因為他死得較早（公元44年），這種可能性似應排除，另外從雅1:1的語氣看，寫信的時候在教會里起主要作用的只有一個雅各而不是兩個。
第二位名叫雅各的使徒是亞勒腓的兒子。聖經裡有四次提到他父親的名字以把他區別出來（太10:3；可3:18；路6:15；徒1:13）。至於他是不是可15:40中的“小雅各”，人們爭論甚多。如果是的話，我們不僅可以知道他的父親是亞勒腓，還可知道他的母親叫馬利亞，有一個兄弟叫約西（太27:56；可15:47；可16:1；路24:10）。可是在另一個地方，這位馬利亞又被稱為革羅罷的妻子（約19:25）。儘管人們試圖通過亞蘭文把革羅罷和亞勒腓統一起來，但這種結論仍然是可疑的。最好還是認定亞勒腓的兒子雅各和小雅各不是一個人。
除了上述的雅各以外，四福音還提到了另一位雅各。他是耶穌的四個兄弟中第一個提到，因而可以假定為長子（太13:55；可6:3）。象小雅各一樣，他也有一個兄弟叫約西，他們的母親（可以說是繼母，見太12:46）是馬利亞。這兩個雅各不大可能是一個人。不大可能稱耶穌的母親為“雅各和約西的母親馬利亞”（太27:56）。此外耶穌的兄弟僅在加1:19中確實地出現。保羅說，他悔改後第一次訪問耶路撒冷時，在所有的使徒中他只見到嘰法（彼得）和“主的兄弟雅各”。
但在《新約》的其他地方，提到了一位叫做雅各的教會領袖，其他地方均未說明他的身份。在使徒行傳中，他第一次處於突出地位是在西庇太的兒子殉身以後。此後顯然只有一位雅各是作用非常突出的領袖。對於他的其他情況沒有作進一步的說明。後來提到這位雅各均表明他是一位舉足輕重的人物。彼得從希律的監獄中被救出來之後，他特地向雅各彙報他得救的經過（徒12:17）。雅各曾主持耶路撒冷會議並宣佈會議的決議（徒15:13,19）。保羅曾向雅各彙報他的工作（徒21:18）。雅各授權給訪問各教會的人（加2:9）。耶穌復活以後可能曾特別向這位雅各顯現，也許對他今後的職責作出特別的指示（林前5:7）。保羅說他是教會三根柱石之首（加2:9）。從各方面因素來考慮，這位雅各最有可能向各教會自稱是“作上帝和主耶穌基督僕人的雅各”（雅1:1）。
但這位雅各是亞勒腓的兒子還是主的兄弟呢？有利於說他是亞勒腓兒子的事實是：一位身列十二使徒之中的雅各，居然很快從記錄中消失，甚至沒有提到他的死，而另一位雅各則不經任何介紹就出現在顯著的地位上，這似乎是不合情理的（徒1:13,14；徒12:17）。在另一方面，有一些證據則有利於證明這位雅各是耶穌的兄弟。保羅在加拉太2章中提到教會的領袖雅各，是在加拉太1章中提到主的兄弟雅各以後不久，雖不能確證，但給人的印象是這兩個地方指的是同一個人。此外，約瑟弗斯所記主的兄弟雅各之死的故事，暗示他是教會的一位領袖（約瑟弗斯《猶太古代史》卷二十9.1）。此外，至少可以追溯到公元二世紀的基督教傳統說法也說，耶路撒冷的教會領袖雅各就是主的兄弟（尤西比烏《教會史》卷二23頁）。
早期的基督教作者關於這封書信的作者眾說紛紜，莫衷一是。他們的錯誤主要在於把亞勒腓的兒子雅各和約西的兄弟雅各當作一個人，或根據靠不住的結論：說加1:19和加2:9的雅各是一個人。
約瑟弗斯說到“那稱為基督的耶穌的兄弟”雅各的死發生在腓斯都死後阿比納斯繼任之前（公元62年）。雅各是被石頭打死的（《猶太古事史》卷二十9.1）。從字面上看這似乎是約西的兄弟雅各死況的真實記錄，但尤西比烏卻把這用在耶路撒冷的領袖，“正義者”雅各身上，引用了另一段在任何已知的約瑟弗斯的著作找不到的文字（《教會史》卷二23）。
尤西比烏還說，聖書表明那位先從基督和眾使徒那裡接受耶路撒冷監督職務的雅各就是“基督的一個兄弟”（同上卷七19）。他以聖經作為權威。他還說保羅認為“正義者”雅各就是“主的兄弟”雅各（同上卷二1），再一次作出超越他所依據材料的推測。但是在另一個地方尤西比烏又說雅各據說是救主的兄弟之一，暗示他為七十門徒之一。他稱雅各為“主的兄弟”，“約瑟的兒子”和“正義者”（同上），還說雅各是耶路撒冷陷落以前不久殉身的（公元70年），革羅罷的兒子西緬（有人說是救主的表兄弟）繼承雅各擔任耶路撒冷的監督（同上卷三11），所以關於雅各的死期，他與約瑟弗斯的說法是矛盾的。他還提到西緬是革羅罷的兒子，猶大是基督的親兄弟（同上卷三19,20,22,32）。他引用赫吉西帕斯的話來支持自己關於西緬是革羅罷的兒子，革羅罷是耶穌叔叔的結論（同上卷三32）。他還用赫吉西帕斯的話說西緬是雅各的表兄弟（同上卷四22）。他引用了赫吉西帕斯關於雅各生與死的著名記錄，儘管根據上下文，這段記錄顯而易見是歪曲事實，大大誇張了的（同上卷二23）。
尤西比烏引用克萊門特的話支持自己關於兩個雅各的說法：一位是“正義者”雅各，是被用漂洗工的棍子打死的，另一位是被砍頭的（同上卷二1）。他說第一位是主的兄弟，儘管克萊門特沒有這樣說。在同一章中他引用克萊門特的話說：“彼得，（西比太的兒子）雅各和約翰在主昇天之後不再爭奪榮譽了，因為他們已經得到了救主所賜的尊榮。他們選正義者雅各為耶路撒冷的監督。”
外傳《希伯來人福音》記載正義者雅各曾發誓從主喝杯到見主復活這段時間裡不吃飯，這裡顯然把他列入出席主晚餐的十二位門徒之中。關於耶穌向他顯現是這樣記載的：耶穌“拿起餅來，祝福了，掰開遞給正義者雅各說：‘我的兄弟，吃了你的餅吧，因為人子已經從死裡復活了。’”這裡“我的兄弟”的稱呼被人理解為這位雅各是主的兄弟。顯然，這類聖經以外的材料對於確定雅各書作者的身份是沒有多大幫助的。
說雅各書為主的兄弟所著，最大的問題也許是書信的語言和文體表明作者有相當的希臘文學寫作能力，不僅詞彙豐富，而且明顯帶有希臘諷刺文學的風格──這是一種普遍的倫理性講辭。主的兄弟不大會有寫出這樣作品的背景。他是加利利木匠的兒子，顯然只熟悉猶太的文化，但在這一點上是不能下結論的，因為有關的爭論所依據的多為不知道的材料，而非已知的材料。
總之，《雅各書》的作者問題仍然是一個不解之謎。也許作者是《新約》中其他地方提到的三位主要的雅各中的一位。
**三、歷史背景**
書信中的許多地理名詞暗示寫信的地點是巴勒斯坦。可以推測作者住在盛產油，酒和無花果的地方，但離海不遠。附近有一些又鹹又苦的水泉。這裡常常乾旱，雨水是非常重要的。
沒有辦法確定寫信的年代。如上所述，寫信的時候教會里似乎只有一位起主要作用的雅各，所以應該是公元44年西庇太的兒子雅各殉身以後。信內的證據表明寫信時間較早，因沒提到任何較大的外邦基督徒團體，或與外邦人有關的問題。教會仍設在會堂裡，但基督教卻已廣泛傳播（徒2:9-11；徒4:36；徒9:2,10,14,19,26；徒11:19:20）。書信的大意是：基督教是所有猶太真信仰的頂峰。
**四、主題**
這是一封有關基督教信仰實際的書信，說明真正活潑的信仰會在信徒生活上產生什麼結果和行為。信中側重於對比真假信仰的表現和結果。這封講道式的書信充滿優美動人的例證，文體簡樸而又直率，層次分明，條理清楚但又顯不出刻意編排的痕跡。他心有所觸，就隨意地把講題表述出來，信中多處引用福山寶訓的內容，茲羅列部分如下：
